newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts hail Roche's first-half sales.
newsitem.headline: Analysts hail Roche's first-half sales.

text.p: Analysts praised Roche Holding AG's first-half sales jump, saying the six percent advance in local-currency terms should help the company's participation certificates advance in the short term.
Certicates were up 35 Swiss francs to 14,320 around 0945 GMT, off a high of 14,435. Sales rose 20 percent in Swiss franc terms to 9.3 billion francs.
"I would say overall these are encouraging results. Certainly they are an improvement on the first quarter, which is good," Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Genghis Lloyd-Harris said from London.
"Pharmaceuticals were slightly stronger than we had expected, but there really is nothing that leaps off the page here," he said.
Zurich Cantonal Bank analyst Meinrad Gyr also seized on the pharmaceutical sales, which rose six percent in local currency and 20 percent in Swiss francs as well.

"After pharmaceuticals rose only three percent in local currencies in the first quarter, second-quarter growth must have been nine percent. (This is) a significant improvement, but not yet the level of Novartis," he wrote in a research note.
He upgraded Roche to to buy from market performer.
Gilbert Puder, chief analyst at Bank Sarasin in Basle, said the results were clearly above his expectations.
"This is especially true in the pharmaceuticals sector, in which we clearly had a pick-up in sales in the second quarter which could have amounted to about nine percent in local currencies," he said.
He said sales growth of around 18 percent was possible in second half, but he noted the weak Swiss franc was distorting the headline number.

"I think the share price short term will be above market," he said, although he added relative performance was difficult to gauge when the Swiss market was already so high in historical terms and from a valuation point of view.
